**Method 1**

When we multiply a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always the sum of squares of the real part and the imaginary part.

For the given complex number $z=-6+\text{i},$ the real part is $\text{Re}(z)=6,$ and the imaginary part is $\text{Im}(z)=1,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(\text{Re}(z))^{2}+(\text{Im}(z))^{2} \\  & =(-6)^{2}+{1}^{2} \\  & =36+1 \\  & =37.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of multiplying the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=-6+\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=-6-\text{i}.$

Multiplying, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(-6+\text{i})(-6-\text{i}) \\  & =(-6)^{2}+(-6)(-1)\text{i}+(1)(-6)\text{i}-{\text{i}}^{2}(1)^{2} \\  & =36+\cancel{6\text{i}}-\cancel{6\text{i}}-(-1)(1) \\  & =36+1 \\  & =37.\end{aligned}
$$
